A1.justification: Both PDFs are complete, readable eight-page versions of the same Generalization Stress Tests study. The main text, four figures, numerical tables, and Appendices A–D support reliable comparison despite the changed title.

before.justification: v1 reports original evaluations of Qwen2.5, Llama3.1, and GPT4o models under controlled benchmark perturbations, including supplementary experiments in the appendices.

after.justification: v2 retains those original empirical results and adds evaluations in which all answer options are lengthened.

M1.justification: The option-rewriting procedure, paired Boolean judgments, and noun-replacement procedure remain unchanged in Section 2 and Appendices A–B. The added all-options-longer experiment uses the existing rewriting mechanism as an additional evaluation control.

E1.justification: On the existing MMLU and ARC-C tasks, v2 additionally evaluates inputs with every answer choice lengthened together (AL). This modestly extends the tested perturbation scenarios; benchmark, domain, and task-family coverage otherwise remains unchanged.

E2.justification: No comparison model is added or removed from a matched experiment. The new AL experiment uses five already evaluated Qwen2.5 and Llama3.1 variants, while the original comparisons, including GPT4o and GPT4o mini, remain intact.

E3.justification: Appendix D.1 adds an AL control evaluated alongside the original, right-option-longer, and wrong-option-longer conditions for five models on two benchmarks. The existing five-shot harness protocol, metrics, and reported settings are unchanged.

E4.justification: The new Appendix D.1/Table 6 examines sensitivity when every option is lengthened, supplementing the existing selective-lengthening and length-control analyses. The earlier all-wrong-options-longer analysis is retained as Appendix D.2/Table 7, with unchanged results.

E5.justification: Neither version reports repeated-run counts, seeds, confidence intervals, or formal significance tests. Point-score reporting and the 100-example manual verification yielding 99% rewriting accuracy remain unchanged.

E6.justification: v2 Table 6 adds ten AL accuracy values and associated model-family and size comparisons. For example, Qwen2.5 1.5B scores 54.7% on MMLU and 67.3% on ARC-C under AL. All original values in Tables 1–5 and v1 Table 6, now Table 7, are unchanged.

T1.justification: Neither version introduces formal theorems or proofs. The informal reasoning supporting paired Boolean judgments and the existing task definitions remain unchanged.

C1.justification: Both versions introduce Generalization Stress Tests and claim that minor perturbations expose accuracy losses and reliance on superficial cues. The revised title, abstract, and conclusion retain these scientific claims and the same headline numerical examples.

C2.justification: The new Section 3.4 repeats the existing explanation that models rely on irrelevant patterns, and the AL discussion reiterates the length-bias interpretation. The limitation excluding chain-of-thought models such as O1 is unchanged. New model-family and size comparisons are empirical findings rather than new mechanism explanations.

D1.justification: Appendix A.1 newly specifies that option-generation settings other than the already reported temperature of zero use defaults. This is additional disclosure, without evidence of changed settings. Prompts, noun-replacement parameters, hardware, and the approximately 1,000 GPU-hour budget remain unchanged.

R1.justification: v2 adds Chen et al. (2023) and Ye et al. (2023) to the benchmark-validity discussion and references. It also expands its criticism of earlier evaluations to include approaches that completely change the original problems; the broader research positioning remains intact.

P1.justification: v2 retitles the paper, rewrites and shortens the abstract and conclusion, reorders the introductory perturbation list, and makes localized wording corrections. It adds a one-sentence Section 3.4 and reorganizes Appendix D, while retaining most methodological and experimental prose.

P2.justification: v2 adds Table 6 with an AL column alongside repeated original/RL/WL results, and renumbers and repositions the previous appendix table as Table 7. The four figures and main-table designs are retained, with modest page reflow.

improvement.justification: The added AL control provides a useful reference for interpreting selective option-lengthening effects, modestly strengthening the empirical analysis while preserving all earlier evidence. However, Appendix D.1 overgeneralizes the model-size trend: under AL, Llama3.1 70B loses 2.8 MMLU points versus 1.2 for 8B. This limits the strength of the added interpretation and the overall improvement.
